title: Time and uncertainty
blurb: Why the length of your wait changes how much risk makes sense, and why honest projections are ranges.
t1.title: How long can you wait?
t1.hook: Asha has two goals: a phone in one year, and a shop deposit in fifteen years. Your mission: see why the wait changes everything.
t1.define: Your **time horizon** is how long it is until you need the money.
t1.analogy: A short trip leaves no time to wait out a storm. A long trip does, though you may still hit rough weather.
q1.opt.a: How long it is until you need the money
q1.opt.b: How much the money will grow
q1.opt.d: How much you put in each month
q1.hint: Think of the length of the trip.
q1.explain: A time horizon is the length of time until you need the money.
q2.prompt: Which of Asha's goals has more time to recover from a fall?
q2.opt.a: The shop deposit in fifteen years
q2.explain: The longer goal has more time to wait out a fall.
t2.title: Watch the range change
t2.define: A longer wait changes the picture. Falls get time to recover, but good and bad outcomes also spread further apart.
t2.explore: Open the lab. Pick the Bumpy Ride, then slide the years from 1 up to 20. Watch each box.
q3.prompt: As the years grow, what happens to the share of futures that end below what you put in, for the Bumpy Ride?
q3.opt.a: It gets smaller, but it does not reach zero
q3.opt.b: It reaches zero, so waiting guarantees a gain
q3.fb.b: Even after 20 years, some futures still end below what you put in. Waiting helps, but it never guarantees a gain.
q3.hint: Read the last box in the lab at 1 year, then at 20 years.
q3.explain: Waiting shrinks the share of losing futures, but some remain, even after 20 years.
q4.prompt: As the years grow, what happens to the gap between the bad case and the good case, in rupees?
q4.hint: Subtract the bad case from the good case at 1 year and at 20 years.
q4.explain: A longer wait lets outcomes spread further apart, so the range gets wider in rupees.
q5.prompt: Compare the Steady Box and the Bumpy Ride at 5 years. Which has the wider range?
q5.hint: Switch paths in the lab and keep the years at 5.
q5.explain: The Bumpy Ride swings more, so its range is wider at every length of wait.
t3.title: Numbers over time
t3.define: Without any swings, growth is just compounding. Money grown at a steady rate for **n** years becomes the start amount times (1 + rate) multiplied by itself n times.
t3.note: Real paths swing around a steady line like this one. The steady line is a way to feel the numbers, not a promise.
q6.prompt: If {amt} grew a steady {rate} a year with no swings, what would it become after {years} years? Type a number in rupees.
q6.hint: Multiply {amt} by 1.10, {years} times. A calculator helps.
q6.explain: {amt} grown at {rate} a year for {years} years becomes about {grown}.
q7.prompt: Use the Rule of 72. At {r72}% a year, about how many years does money take to double? Type a number.
t4.title: Honest projections
t4.define: No one can promise a single number. An honest **projection** is a range, and it states its **assumptions**, the guesses it is built on.
t4.tradeoff: A shorter wait needs less risk, because there is less time to recover. A longer wait can take more, but it is never guaranteed.
q8.prompt: A website says: you will have exactly ₹10 lakh in 10 years. What is missing?
q8.opt.a: A range, and the assumptions it is built on
q8.opt.b: Nothing, it is a promise you can rely on
q8.opt.d: A picture of a rupee note
q8.fb.b: No one can promise a single number. An honest projection shows a range and its assumptions.
q8.hint: Remember the range in the lab.
q8.explain: A single exact number hides the uncertainty. An honest projection shows a range and its assumptions.
q9.prompt: A fund grew 20% a year for 3 years. What can you say?
q9.opt.a: Past results do not promise future ones
q9.opt.b: It will do the same again
q9.fb.b: Good years in the past do not repeat on demand. They tell you nothing certain about the next years.
q9.hint: Can anyone promise that a past pattern will repeat?
q9.explain: Past results do not promise future ones.
glossary.time_horizon.def: How long it is until you need the money.
glossary.projection.def: A guess about the future, honestly shown as a range.
glossary.assumption.def: A guess a projection is built on, such as a growth rate.
